title: A fresh Idempotency-Key is made on every click, so retrying an unconfirmed refund can refund twice
evidence: api.js:32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeated request 'for the same attempt'. app.js:128 generates a new key inside refundSelected on each click. On failure (app.js:131-133) the selection is kept, the button is re-enabled in the finally block (app.js:135-136) and no load() runs. A retry therefore sends a different key. state.refunding only guards double-clicks while a request is in flight.
failing_case: The user clicks Refund and confirms. The server processes the refund, but the response is lost (504 or dropped connection). The UI shows 'The refund was not confirmed'. The same rows are still ticked and the button is enabled. The user clicks Refund again and confirms. The second request has a new key, so the server refunds the same orders twice. The on-screen warning to 'check the order statuses' is advice only; nothing stops the retry.
remediation: Keep the key with the pending attempt (same ids) and reuse it for a retry. Discard it only after a confirmed success or when the selection changes. After an unconfirmed failure, reload the list and disable the retry until statuses are fresh.

title: Orders that are already refunded or still pending can be selected and sent for refund
evidence: renderRow (app.js:34-60) adds a live checkbox for every order, whatever its status. selectedOrders (app.js:75) and refundSelected (app.js:119-123) apply no status rule. The confirm total sums o.total for every picked order. The Status column shows 'refunded' for them, so the UI itself says they are not refundable. The requirement is inferred; no document states the rule.

requirement.why: the table has a 'refunded' status and the page offers a 'Refund selected' action, which implies refunded orders should not be refunded again

failing_case: Filter to 'refunded', tick one $120 order and click 'Refund 1 order'. The dialog says 'Refund 1 order totalling $120.00? This sends money back to the customers.' and sends the request. If the server does not reject it, the customer is paid twice. Even if it does reject, the user sees only a generic error.
remediation: Put the 'can this order be refunded' rule in domain.js as a pure function with a test. Disable the checkbox (with a stated reason) for orders that fail it, and exclude them from the selection and the confirm total.

title: The refund response body is never inspected: partial failure shows as full success, and an empty 2xx shows as failure
evidence: api.js:34-38 returns whatever request() parses, and app.js:128 discards it. api.js:17 calls res.json() on every 2xx, including the refund. README.md:13 says success is reported 'only after the server confirms it', but the only confirmation checked is res.ok. Traced. The server contract is not in the payload.
failing_case: (a) Server answers 200 {"refunded":[4],"failed":[7]}: the toast says 'Refunded 2 orders.' although #7 was not refunded, and the reload may hide that. (b) Server answers 204 No Content, a common reply to a POST: res.json() throws, the user sees 'not valid JSON' and 'The refund was not confirmed' for a refund that went through, and likely retries (compounding the idempotency finding).

requirement.why: README.md:13 promises success only after server confirmation; the response contract is not documented

remediation: Define the refund response shape. Validate it in refund(), report per-id results, and treat an empty 2xx as success only if the contract says so.

title: Paging drops keyboard focus onto a disabled button, and the page change is not announced
evidence: renderTable (app.js:62-73) sets prev.disabled / next.disabled after the click. On the last page the focused Next button becomes disabled (same for Previous on page 1), and a disabled button cannot keep keyboard focus. #page (index.html:34) is a plain span, not a live region, and tbody is replaced wholesale (app.js:67). Traced; the page was not run, because Bash was denied.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to Next on page 2 of 3 and presses Enter. Page 3 renders and Next becomes disabled. Focus is lost, the next Tab starts from the top of the document, and a screen-reader user hears nothing about 'Page 3 of 3' or the new rows (WCAG 2.4.3, 4.1.3).
remediation: After renderTable, if the focused pager button is now disabled, move focus to the other pager button or to the table caption (tabindex=-1). Put the 'Page X of Y' text in a role=status region or add it to #message.

title: normaliseOrder turns a missing total into a valid $0.00 order instead of dropping it
evidence: domain.js:7 says the function returns null when there is 'no numeric total', and api.js:28-29 counts such records as skipped. Number(null), Number(""), Number([]) and Number(false) are all 0, and Number(true) is 1, so Number.isFinite at domain.js:12 passes. Traced from JS coercion rules; Bash was denied, so it was not executed.
failing_case: The API returns {"id":"A7","total":null,"status":"paid","customer":{"name":"Ann"}} (an incomplete record). It is shown as $0.00 with no 'could not be shown' note. If the user selects it with a $50 order, the confirm dialog says 'totalling $50.00' while the real amount is unknown. The skipped-record warning never fires. The order is also counted in Orders and in the average.
remediation: Reject null, empty string and non-number types before coercion: require typeof raw.total === 'number' (or a non-empty numeric string) and a non-negative finite value, then count the record as skipped.

quote: const discounted = order.customer.tier === "gold" ? applyBp(cents, 10000 - GOLD_DISCOUNT_BP) : cents;
title: Revenue stat re-applies a gold discount and sales tax to the server's order total
evidence: orderRevenueCents (domain.js:25-30) takes order.total, applies -10% for gold, then +8.25% tax. The refund confirm (app.js:122-123) uses the raw o.total, so the two screens disagree. The server sets and charges the amount; the client holds a second copy of the pricing rule. The summary also averages over every order, including pending and refunded ones that contribute 0 (domain.js:35). The requirement is inferred; no document says whether total is pre- or post-discount.

requirement.why: a field named total from the server is normally the final charged amount

failing_case: A gold customer has a paid order with total 100.00 (already net of discount and tax). Revenue shows $97.43 (90.00 x 1.0825), while the refund dialog for the same order says $100.00. With one paid and one pending order of 100.00, 'Average per order' shows about $48.71 rather than $100.00 for paid ones. If the rates change on the server, the dashboard goes silently wrong.
remediation: Have the API return the net revenue per order, or state in a spec whether total is pre- or post-discount and tax. Sum that figure. Label the average ('per order, all statuses') or divide by paid orders only.

title: After a successful refund the picked orders stay selected if the reload fails, and can be refunded again
evidence: state.selected is cleared only inside the success branch of load() (app.js:98). If load() fails, its own catch (app.js:105-108) swallows the error, so refundSelected shows the 'Refunded' toast (app.js:129) and returns normally. The stale table still lists the orders as paid and still checked, and finally (app.js:110) re-enables the refund button once n > 0. Traced.
failing_case: Refund orders 4 and 7 and the server confirms. The follow-up GET /orders returns 500 or times out. The toast says 'Refunded 2 orders.', then the message line switches to 'Orders could not be loaded.' The table still shows #4 and #7 as paid, checked, with 'Refund 2 orders' enabled. A second click and confirm sends a second refund with a new key (see the idempotency finding).
remediation: Clear state.selected (and mark or remove the refunded ids locally) as soon as refund() resolves, before calling load(). Show the reload failure as its own message instead of leaving the table looking current.

quote: setMessage(`Orders could not be loaded. ${err.message}`, true);
title: A failed search leaves the previous results, stats and selection on screen as if they matched
evidence: The catch block (app.js:105-108) sets only the message. state.orders, state.selected and the table are not cleared, and the finally block (app.js:110) re-enables the Refund button for the old selection.
failing_case: The user ticks two rows, then types 'smith' and the request returns 500. A red line appears above a table that still shows the old rows with 'smith' typed in the box, and 'Refund 2 orders' is still enabled. The user can refund rows that are not the search results.
remediation: On a failed load, clear the rows and selection, or mark the table as stale and disable the refund action until a load succeeds.
